bear.story: Q3/Q4 burn plus ATM selling after the lock-up and/or a dilutive raise near $80-100, TENEX 2027 waiver late or denied, the first capex/capacity disclosure (Investor Day) at or above ~$1,450/SWU-yr; the market moves toward cash + DOE milestones + option (~$35-60).

base.story: Build on track (first Oak Ridge centrifuge, Piketon construction, 2028 DOE milestone in sight) but disclosed economics do not close the gap to the 2025-26 sell-side targets; continued burn and some ATM dilution; EV ~$1.4B as the market keeps paying for scarcity of US enrichment.

bull.story: Investor Day shows >2M SWU initial capacity at <$1,100/SWU-yr or term contracts at $250+, DOE options or NNSA work, sector rebound with ~30% short interest squeezing.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E BWXT 26.9x, CEG 20.4x (peers.md); trailing EV/EBITDA BWXT 25.2x, CEG 14.0x, VST 12.9x (median 14.0x); trailing EV/sales 3.67x-4.67x. Fewer than 10 genuine comparables exist: Centrus is the only listed US enricher; Urenco, Orano and Rosatom are state/utility-owned, General Matter is private; miners and pre-revenue reactor developers were dropped (supervisor comps review, accepted).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: No multiple leg (weight 0): NTM EBITDA at H is negative (FY2028 trough), so EV/EBITDA has nothing to bite on, and round 1's 4.0x EV/sales near the peer median was not justified for resale revenue at a 3.6% TTM EBITDA margin. The market-share leg uses 10x 2035 EBITDA (12x bull) for an owned plant, below the 14.0x trailing median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: 10x is a ~30% discount to the 14.0x peer median: a single-site, first-of-a-kind plant selling a commodity service whose real price is capped by 9M+ SWU of announced Western additions (WNA), against regulated/contracted generators and a defense-anchored fuel manufacturer.

thesis_break_reason: $40 (market cap ~$1.0B on 24.9M shares) is below what the market should pay for the parts that do not depend on the LEU build: net cash at H ~$445M + Westerman $116M + DOE task-order milestones risked PV ~$590M + pension/convert adjustments $70M - transition burn ~$147M = ~$1.07B. Trading there would mean the plant is priced at zero or less - most likely a failed/stalled build (first cascades slipping past 2030, capex blow-out at the first disclosure), lost DOE milestone funding or a distressed raise - not 89%-vol noise. It sits below my bear scenario ($45) and the market-share failure state is ~$13. On the upside, a sustained close above ~$160 would break my view that the stock prices more expansion value than the economics support; it would most likely reflect disclosed capacity/cost (>2M SWU at <$1,100/SWU-yr) or term SWU above $300.

60-day offering lock-up expires; ATM can resume
First Investor Day at Piketon (announced on the Q2 2026 call; no formal notice or date yet): capacity, capex, timeline
First new Oak Ridge centrifuge completed (company milestone)
DOE decision on the 2026-27 TENEX waiver / Russian export licences for 2027 deliveries
FY2027 appropriations: HALEU cascade operation funding (proposed budget does not fund it); DOE options
Russian LEU import waivers end; FY2028 supply gap

key_uncertainties: Expansion capacity and capex per SWU-yr are undisclosed; my ~$1,450 could be 30% off either way (fair value $30-57).
HALEU price basis: whether DOE's $17.0M/MTU includes feed changes the HALEU leg by ~$5/sh.
Term SWU price path once Urenco NEF (+2.8M SWU to 2036), Orano IKE (7.4M SWU) and GLE Paducah (up to 6M SWU) add Western capacity in 2030-36.
TENEX deliveries in 2027 (waiver pending; Russian export licences) and the FY2028 supply gap.
HALEU demand: depends on X-energy, Oklo, Radiant, Antares and TerraPower reaching fuel load.

Financing path: ~$0.85B gap to 2030 (capex after H $1.74B + burn ~$0.21B + 2030 converts $0.40B + ~$0.3B minimum cash vs ~$1.45B gross cash at H before any raise + risked 2028 DOE milestone ~$0.31B); ATM, follow-ons or DOE/EXIM debt.
Defense-adjacent exposure (Antares military microreactors, 'unobligated' national-security output) and Kilian's defense rule.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's findings removed my two highest-value legs: the General Matter mark (aggregator figures, no primary source; weight 0.15 -> 0) and EV/sales 4.0x on low-margin resale revenue (0.10 -> 0). I accepted both, the 21% tax rate (adding back, as a separate $46M adjustment, the bonus-depreciation shield the rNPV cannot see, net of tax on DOE receipts), Westerman's ~$160M revenue (424B5; valued at its $116M price), and a government-payer rate for the DOE milestones (6%; retimed to 40% 2028 / 30% 2031 / 30% at the July 2032 delivery, nothing before H). I disagree on two points: the December Investor Day was announced on the Q2 call (transcript), so it stays a catalyst without a firm date; and I keep HALEU at $375/SWU (41 SWU/kgU x 12 MTU) rather than $350. Phase probabilities now rest on the WNA base rate (ACP 2009, Eagle Rock), not a forum post; option vol cut to 45% with S risked. Engine fair value $42.95 (SOTP $22.99 w0.40, market-share $63.03 w0.30, floor + option $49.50 w0.30; DCF off as FY2028 NOPAT < 0), down from $55.76. The capex per SWU-yr is the swing driver (+/-30% -> $56.5 / $30.3). The ladder is not centred on fair value: the market prices a scarcity premium and the first capex disclosure is the decider, so scenarios are bear $45 (0.35) / base $90 (0.45) / bull $180 (0.20) with ~40% within-scenario vol: median ~$80, mean ~$100, P(>= $109.88) 0.32 (round 1: 0.35). Alternative signals (30% short interest, lock-up end and ATM overhang, -73% from the high) tilt the year and the month slightly below spot. ~9 follow-up searches/fetches; X and Reddit remain unreachable.

model_inputs.structure_note: Fuel-cycle developer in transition: the third year (FY2028) is a forced trough - Russian supply barred after 2027, own Piketon output only from 2029-30 - so FY2028 NOPAT is negative and the engine sets the DCF to 0 (pre-profit year 3); a DCF fading from FY2028 would also shrink the business that the Piketon plant replaces. Value is carried by (1) a SOTP (weight 0.40) built per the playbook's contract-book method: Piketon LEU and HALEU as rNPV parts (SWU x price x margin, phase probabilities, capex as dev costs), the DOE $900M task order as a separate milestone part at 6%, the transition burn as a cash-flow part and Westerman at its transaction price; (2) market-share scenarios (0.30) and (3) cash floor plus option (0.30), both per method_fit. No multiple leg: NTM EBITDA at H is negative, so a finite-life EV/EBITDA has nothing to bite on, and EV/sales on low-margin resale revenue was not justified (supervisor, accepted). General Matter mark at weight 0. Leg weights are judgment, untested. The segment build (FY2026-28) feeds only the net-debt context; expansion capex is kept out of the years and enters through net_debt_horizon (spend before H) and the rNPV dev costs (after H), so it is counted once.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (a) capex ~$1,450/SWU-yr (~$2.6B from mid-2026 for ~1.8M SWU-equivalent) is my estimate - undisclosed; at ~$1,000/SWU-yr fair value rises ~$13.7/sh (+32%) and at +30% it falls ~$12.5/sh: the single driver that moves value most (flagged); (b) leg weights 0.40 / 0.30 / 0.30 are judgment (market-share and option legs carry phase-2 and flexibility value the rNPV omits; each 0.10 shifted from SOTP to option adds ~$2.7/sh); (c) +$46M tax correction (bonus depreciation less tax on DOE receipts), +$1.9/sh, below the flag line; (d) DOE milestones at 6% rather than the 9% project rate (+$0.6/sh on fair value, below the flag line); (e) net_debt_horizon and shares.horizon are stated directly (derivations in inputs_detail) and include a probability-weighted $400M raise (p 0.5); (f) fair value is far below spot ($109.88) and the sell-side average ($240.82, stale): the gap rests mainly on (a), the 45% margin and the SWU deck, all low-to-medium confidence; the first company capex/capacity disclosure (Investor Day, December 2026, per the Q2 call) decides it.
